Done. The response-model serialization options `response_model_exclude_defaults` and `response_model_exclude_none` were missing throughout the stack; I restored them end-to-end.

**Changes**

- `fastapi/encoders.py` — `jsonable_encoder` gained `exclude_defaults` and `exclude_none` (replacing the inverted `include_none`); both are forwarded to `BaseModel.dict()` on pydantic v1 (`exclude_defaults` raises `ValueError` on pydantic <1), `exclude_none` filters `None` dict values, and the flags propagate through recursion.
- `fastapi/routing.py` — `_prepare_response_content` and `serialize_response` accept and apply both flags; `get_request_handler`, `APIRoute` (params, attributes, `get_route_handler`), all `APIRouter` route methods (`add_api_route`, `api_route`, `get`/`put`/`post`/`delete`/`options`/`head`/`patch`/`trace`) expose `response_model_exclude_defaults`/`response_model_exclude_none`; `include_router` propagates them from each route.
- `fastapi/applications.py` — same two parameters added to all `FastAPI` route methods and forwarded to the router.
- `fastapi/openapi/utils.py` — the two `include_none=False` call sites now use `exclude_none=True`, preserving OpenAPI output.

This mirrors upstream FastAPI's implementation of the feature (the `include_none` → `exclude_none` inversion included), so signature consistency between `APIRouter` and `FastAPI` methods is preserved.

**Testing caveat**: the environment has no pydantic/starlette/pytest and no network access, so `pytest` can't run here. I verified by loading the real modified modules with stubbed dependencies and exercising the actual code paths — 15/15 checks pass, covering `jsonable_encoder` flags (including the `exclude_defaults` assertions in `tests/test_jsonable_encoder.py`), `serialize_response`, app-level decorators, and router-level options surviving `include_router`.
